What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 1

    Discover

    1–2 weeks

    We walk the student and parent journey with admissions, academic, transport, accounts and support staff, map where enquiries, messages and approvals pile up, and review what the ERP, LMS and test platform can expose. We also review consent forms, the privacy notice, the WhatsApp groups in use and current advertising claims.

    Deliverables

    • Journey map with failure points for each segment you run
    • Systems and data inventory with integration options
    • Consent, children's data and channel policy gap review
    • Prioritized automation backlog with effort ranges

    What we need from you

    • ERP, LMS or test platform administrator and API documentation or vendor contact
    • Current admission forms, consent wording, privacy notice and message templates
    • Anonymized monthly volumes for enquiries, attendance exceptions and fee follow-ups
    • Named owners: principal or director, admissions head, IT head and accounts officer
  2. 2

    Design

    1–2 weeks

    We design flows, templates, routing rules and data flows, including the sensitive-message script for ragging, harassment and distress and the parent consent flow for under-18 learners. Academic content, fee and refund terms and consent wording are written or approved by your team, not by us.

    Deliverables

    • Conversation flows and template drafts for WhatsApp approval and DLT registration
    • Parent consent and age-gate design for under-18 learners
    • Sensitive-message routing rules for leadership sign-off
    • Data flow diagram with retention and access for each field

    What we need from you

    • Consent and notice wording reviewed by your legal or compliance owner
    • Sign-off on routing rules by the principal, dean of students or academic head
    • WhatsApp Business account, display name and DLT entity registration access
  3. 3

    Build

    2–4 weeks

    We build the integrations in n8n and the agreed tools against a test environment with synthetic student data, set up the consent log, staff queues and dashboards, and document every connection and credential owner.

    Deliverables

    • Working integrations in a test environment
    • Consent and purpose log covering parents and adult students
    • Staff queues and dashboards
    • Integration documentation and access list

    What we need from you

    • Sandbox or test access to the ERP, LMS or test platform
    • Sample timetables, fee structures and handbook documents
    • Staff time for weekly build reviews
  4. 4

    Validate & launch

    1–2 weeks

    We test with counselors, teachers, transport and accounts staff, run scripted cases such as an absent child whose parent did not know, a ragging report or a fee dispute, fix what fails, and launch in one campus, grade band, program or batch before any wider rollout.

    Deliverables

    • Test report including sensitive-message script results
    • Go-live checklist and rollback plan
    • Staff training and quick reference guides
    • Operating runbook

    What we need from you

    • Go-live approval from the principal or registrar and the data protection contact
    • Staff available for training and the first live week
  5. 5

    Operate & improve

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    We monitor failed messages, template quality, handoffs and model accuracy, review KPIs with your owners each month and before each admission season, and change content and rules only through an approved change process.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly KPI and quality review
    • Failure and incident log with fixes
    • Pre-season admissions readiness check
    • Change log for templates, rules and prompts

    What we need from you

    • Named owner for change approvals
    • Monthly review time with academic and operations leads

First pilot: Four-week admissions desk pilot

Start with one campus, grade band, program or center. Enquiries from your ads, website and walk-ins land in one CRM, get an approved acknowledgment and a named counselor, and families book tours or demos on WhatsApp while counselors keep every conversation. We compare first response time and enquiry-to-visit conversion with earlier weeks. Out of season, absence alerts make a good alternative start.

  • One campus, grade band, program or center on an approved WhatsApp number
  • Lead capture from Meta, Google, the website and walk-in QR codes into one CRM
  • Acknowledgment, tour or demo booking and reminder templates approved by Meta and your admissions head
  • Counselor assignment with escalation to the admissions head
  • Baseline and pilot comparison of first response time and enquiry-to-visit conversion

Ways to work together

Choose the engagement that fits your stage.

  • Pilot sprint

    One automation, one segment and one accountable owner. We build, validate and measure it against agreed acceptance criteria before anything wider is committed.

    Best for: Proving value and fit with low risk

  • Phased rollout

    A prioritized roadmap across the journey, released in reviewed increments, with training and documentation after each release.

    Best for: Teams ready to connect several workflows

  • Operate & improve

    Monthly reviews of measures and exceptions, template and rule updates, and new automations as priorities change, during business hours.

    Best for: Keeping automations accurate as the business changes

Safe by design, owned by your team

  • Parents first: an under-18 learner's data is processed only with recorded, verifiable parental consent or under an exemption that clearly applies, and messages about a child go only to registered parent numbers.
  • No automated decisions about students: AI may draft, classify, extract and summarize, but admissions, grades, concessions, discipline and refunds stay with the authorized staff member.
  • No profiling or targeting of children: behavioral nudges and ad audiences are built only from adults who opted in, and child accounts are excluded from both.
  • Sensitive-message testing on every change: a ragging, harassment, distress and emergency script approved by the principal or dean of students runs before each release of templates, rules or prompts.
  • Minimum data in messages: notifications carry no marks, health, disciplinary or fee comparisons, and documents open only behind expiring links with one-time codes.
  • Role-based access, processing logs kept at least one year as the DPDP Rules require, quarterly access reviews, AI providers under enterprise terms without training on student data, and a breach runbook for informing families and the Data Protection Board.

The obligations that shape the design

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

  • DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025 on children's data

    Anyone under eighteen is a child. Institutions need verifiable consent from a parent confirmed as an identifiable adult, and may not track, behaviorally monitor or target ads at children. The Rules exempt educational institutions only for tracking needed for educational activities or enrolled children's safety, and school transport providers only for location during travel. These duties apply from May 2027 as notified; MeitY has consulted on an earlier date.

    meity.gov.in · Source

  • Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009

    In admissions covered by the Act, Section 13 bars capitation fees and any screening of a child or parents other than random selection, Section 14 bars refusing admission for lack of age proof, and Section 12(1)(c) requires private unaided schools to admit at least a quarter of their entry class from disadvantaged groups and weaker sections through the state's process. Our workflows never score or rank children or parents.

    indiacode.nic.in · Source

  • Ministry of Education Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Center, 2024

    Circulated to states in January 2024 for adoption through their own laws, the guidelines expect registration, a website listing tutor qualifications, courses, fees and refund policy, no misleading promises of ranks or marks, no enrollment below sixteen, pro-rata refunds when a student leaves mid-course, and support for well-being. Several states, including Haryana, Rajasthan and Jharkhand, have since passed laws or rules, so workflows follow each state's version.

    education.gov.in · Source

  • Consumer rules on coaching advertising and online selling

    The Central Consumer Protection Authority's 2024 coaching guidelines, which also cover online coaching, bar false claims about courses, faculty, fees, refunds, success rates and ranks, require a successful candidate's written consent before using their name, photo or testimonial, and require prominent disclosures. Its 2023 dark pattern guidelines list false urgency, subscription traps and drip pricing. Your legal adviser reviews our templates and checkouts against both.

    pib.gov.in · Source

  • UGC and AICTE rules on refunds, original certificates, ragging and grievances

    UGC's fee refund policy, and AICTE's for technical programs, govern refunds when students withdraw, and institutions must verify original certificates and return them immediately rather than retain them. Students and parents file an online anti-ragging undertaking each year, and UGC's 2023 grievance regulations require an online portal, a Students' Grievance Redressal Committee and an Ombudsperson. Our workflows route to these processes.

    ugc.gov.in · Source

  • WhatsApp policy and TRAI rules for family messaging

    WhatsApp requires opt-in, approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window and a clear route to a person, and since January 2026 its terms allow AI for a business's own support, not general-purpose assistants. SMS and calls in India follow TRAI's TCCCPR: registered DLT headers and templates, separate promotional and service categories, an opt-out in promotional messages under the 2025 amendment, and no new consent request for ninety days after an opt-out.

    business.whatsapp.com · Source

Frequently asked

Will an AI chatbot answer parents and students on our behalf?

Only for routine questions, and only from content your team approves, such as the prospectus, fee schedule, handbook or help center, with a citation to the source. Anything about a specific child's marks, discipline, health or fees, and every grievance, ragging report or sign of distress, goes to a named person. Your principal, dean of students or learner success lead signs off the routing rules and the sensitive-message test script before launch.

Do we need to replace our school ERP, LMS or coaching app?

No. We connect to the systems you already run through their APIs, vendor integrations or approved exports, and your ERP remains the record for admissions, attendance, fees and results. Where a system offers no interface, we agree a safe interim route such as scheduled exports and state its limits clearly.

Can we keep using class WhatsApp groups?

You can, but official communication moves to a WhatsApp Business number and the parent app: each parent receives messages individually, numbers are not exposed to other parents, and acknowledgments are recorded. Groups can stay for informal class updates if the school wishes, under its own moderation policy.

How do you handle children's data under the DPDP Act?

We design for the DPDP Act and Rules: verifiable parental consent for under-18s, no behavioral tracking or targeted advertising directed at children, and only the narrow educational and safety tracking the Rules permit for schools and their transport providers. The children's provisions apply from May 2027 under the notified schedule, though MeitY has consulted on an earlier date, so we build for them now. Your legal or compliance owner reviews the consent wording. Nothing on this page is legal advice.

Will automated fee reminders upset parents?

They are designed not to. Reminders go privately to the registered fee payer, use wording your principal or registrar approves, stop after an agreed number, and always offer a way to request an installment plan or speak to accounts. Children, class groups and teachers never see who owes fees.

Can you help a coaching institute keep its advertising and results claims safe?

We build workflows that keep claims factual: result posts drawn only from candidates who gave written consent after their results, disclosures placed beside every claim, and follow-up templates reviewed by your legal adviser. We do not approve legal claims ourselves, and no message we build promises selections or ranks.

We are an international school or sell courses abroad. Does that change anything?

It can. In the US, COPPA covers online services directed at children under thirteen, and its amended rule has required compliance since April 2026, while FERPA governs education records at institutions funded by the US Department of Education. If you offer services to people in the EU, the GDPR may apply alongside the DPDP Act. We scope these requirements with your legal team during discovery.

How long does a first project take, and what drives the cost?

A first pilot usually runs three to six weeks, depending mainly on ERP access and template approvals, and we plan admissions work ahead of your season. We quote after discovery, once your systems, volumes and existing licenses are known. Provider charges such as WhatsApp messaging, SMS and model usage are billed by those providers and shown separately.
